summary.headline: A holding company at a discount to its parts, but the parts earn less than their cost of capital: fair value about Rs 59.40
summary.text: Vallibel One PLC (VONE.N0000) holds 51.75% of LB Finance, 55.98% of Royal Ceramics, 14.95% of Sampath Bank, 68.75% of Delmege, the unfinished Greener Water hotel and, since October, just over half of The Fortress Resorts; the holding company itself has no debt. Year to March 2026: revenue Rs 149.3bn (+22%), profit to owners Rs 13.17bn (+12%), EPS Rs 11.57, dividend Rs 3.00. The first half of this year was better again: EPS Rs 4.93 against Rs 4.03 (+22%), led by LB Finance. At Rs 91.30 (CSE close, 20 November 2026) the share is 7.3x trailing EPS of Rs 12.47 and 0.83x NAV of Rs 110.29, and about 9% below what its stakes are worth at market prices (about Rs 100 a share). But owners' ROE has been only 10–12.5% for three years against an 18.3% cost of equity (beta 0.98). On four methods (sum of the parts, P/E, justified P/B, residual income) the fair value is about Rs 59.40, so the price is about 54% above it. I'd buy at up to Rs 50.50 and treat under Rs 44.60 as a strong buy. It passes 2 of the 4 business tests (debt and steady profit; it fails on returns and cash), so it stays in category 3, avoid for now. Mr Dhammika Perera and two Vallibel companies own 80.4%; nothing moved among the big holders between June and September.

fullText:
**Summary**

Vallibel One PLC (VONE.N0000) is Mr Dhammika Perera's holding company. Its value sits in three listed stakes and a handful of private businesses: 51.75% of LB Finance (the biggest piece, about 41% of the parts at market prices), 55.98% of Royal Ceramics (tiles, bathware, which owns a further 26.08% of LB Finance), 14.95% of Sampath Bank, 68.75% of Delmege (consumer and trading), 100% of Greener Water (an unfinished hotel project) and, since October 2026, just over half of The Fortress Resorts. The holding company itself has no debt and about Rs 3.9bn of cash and deposits.

Results are strong and rising. Year to March 2026: revenue Rs 149.3bn (+22%), profit to owners Rs 13.17bn (+12%), EPS Rs 11.57, dividend Rs 3.00. Six months to September 2026: EPS Rs 4.93 against Rs 4.03 (+22%), driven by LB Finance (segment profit +27%) after it bought Associated Motor Finance. NAV is Rs 110.29.

At Rs 91.30 (CSE close, 20 November 2026) the share is 7.3x trailing EPS of Rs 12.47 and 0.83x NAV. That looks cheap, and it is about 9% below what the parts are worth at market prices (about Rs 100 a share). But the group earns only about 11–12% on owners' equity, well under the 18.3% a shareholder should demand at a beta of 0.98, and Royal Ceramics is itself valued by this site well below its own price. On four methods the fair value is about **Rs 59.40** (Rs 60.50 on 16 November). I'd buy at up to **Rs 50.50** and treat under **Rs 44.60** as a strong buy. The business passes 2 of 4 tests (debt, steady profit; it fails returns and cash), so it stays **category 3, avoid for now**.

**What changed in this redo (20 November 2026)**

The research record was rebuilt from the same three reports (annual report 2025/26, interims to June and September 2026), adding the management and shareholder sections, group capex booked (Rs 5.79bn in 2025/26, Rs 5.83bn in 2024/25) and the half-year segment figures. The price moves from the 30 September close (Rs 88.80) to the 20 November CSE close (Rs 91.30). Residual income is now calculated by the site's valuation code (ROE moving in a straight line from 11.8% to its long-run level, payout 26% throughout): Rs 45.7 instead of the hand-worked Rs 49.9. That is the only reason the fair value falls, by Rs 1.10. No other assumption changed.

**Valuation table (Rs per share)**

| Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sum of the parts | 53.3 | 82.5 | 118.2 | 80.9 |
| P/E | 42.7 | 53.5 | 67.9 | 53.2 |
| Justified P/B | 45.4 | 58.1 | 76.6 | 58.0 |
| Residual income | 34.2 | 45.5 | 63.2 | 45.7 |
| **Average** | **43.9** | **59.9** | **81.5** | **59.4** |

Weights bear 30 / base 50 / bull 20. Buy price = fair value less 15% (Rs 50.50), strong buy = less 25% (Rs 44.60).

**What the company owns (30 September 2026)**

- LB Finance PLC: 286.73mn shares (51.75% direct; 66.34% effective with Royal Ceramics' 26.08%). Profit Rs 14.04bn in 2025/26, equity Rs 63.3bn, ROE about 24%. Worth Rs 45.6bn at Rs 159 (broker table, 9 November).
- Royal Ceramics Lanka PLC: 620.03mn shares (55.98%). Worth Rs 28.0bn at Rs 45.10 (CSE close, 20 November). This site values it at Rs 27.20 a share (category 3).
- Sampath Bank PLC: 175.35mn shares (14.95%), carried at Rs 24.5bn (Rs 140.00) in September; Rs 26.0bn at Rs 148.25 (CSE close, 20 November). This site values it at Rs 186.
- Unlisted: Delmege (68.75%, cost Rs 2.65bn, Vallibel One's share of profit Rs 1.00bn in 2025/26), Greener Water (100%, cost Rs 7.35bn, hotel completion "further extended"), Swisstek Aluminium (37.56% direct, cost Rs 0.49bn), Vallibel One Properties.
- The Fortress Resorts PLC: 18.59% at March (market value Rs 0.45bn); bought up to 50.74% (53.33% with the group) on 21–22 October 2026. The cost isn't in the reports, and it was paid after the September balance sheet, so it is in neither the cash nor the stake value used here.
- Holding-company cash and short-term investments Rs 3.99bn, lease liabilities Rs 0.12bn.

**Methods**

*Sum of the parts.* The natural method for a holding company. LB Finance isn't covered by this site, so it's valued on its own book value at a justified price to book (its ROE is about 20–24%, beta 0.97, cost of equity about 18.2%): 0.82x / 1.15x / market. Royal Ceramics and Sampath use this site's own bear/base/bull values, so the views stay consistent. The holding-company discount is 20% / 10% / 0%: the holding company's running costs are covered by the technical fees it charges, so the discount stands for control (the Perera family and related companies own about 80%; 19.5% is public) and profit kept in the subsidiaries. Result Rs 53.3 / 82.5 / 118.2.

*P/E.* Base EPS Rs 12.20 for 2026/27 (H1 Rs 4.93 + Rs 7.30), 2% below the Rs 12.47 run-rate. The bear (Rs 10.90) is 13% below, because the September quarter (Rs 2.51) annualises to only Rs 10.04 and LB Finance booked a Rs 1.9bn impairment of receivables. Justified forward P/E at the cost of equity 3.9x / 4.4x / 5.1x. Result Rs 42.7 / 53.5 / 67.9.

*Justified P/B and residual income.* Owners' ROE has been 10–12.5% for three years (18.9% in 2021/22). Long-run ROE 10.5% / 12% / 13.5% against a cost of equity of 19.8% / 18.3% / 16.8% means kept profit earns less than shareholders require, so book value is worth less than its face: 0.41x–0.69x NAV, and residual income Rs 34.2 / 45.5 / 63.2. Both use a long-run ROE well below the 15% benchmark; that is right for this group because the Sampath stake (carried at market, yielding about 6%) and the idle Greener Water investment sit in equity without earning much.

*Dividends.* Rs 3.00 a year for two years (Rs 1.00 and nothing in the two years before): a 26% payout and a 3.3% yield. A further Rs 1.50 a share was paid in the June 2026 quarter; the reports don't say which year it is for. A dividend model gives only Rs 20–29 because three-quarters of profit is kept, so it isn't in the average. The dividend itself is safe: the holding company received Rs 4.14bn of dividends in 2025/26 (Rs 2.22bn in this half) against Rs 3.42bn paid.

*DCF.* Not used. The consolidated cash flow is dominated by LB Finance's lending (loans +Rs 45.7bn in this half alone), so a whole-company DCF would be meaningless; the operating businesses are valued by a DCF inside this site's Royal Ceramics analysis, which feeds the sum of the parts. Group capex booked was Rs 5.8bn last year against Rs 4.0bn of depreciation, mostly in the tile factories.

**Required return**

Cost of equity = 8.24% + 0.98 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.3% (bear 19.8%, bull 16.8%). Risk-free = 12.24% bond yield − 4.0% default spread. Beta 0.98 (provisional): the value-weighted average of LB Finance 0.97 (finance companies), Royal Ceramics 1.12 (this site's figure), Sampath 0.70 (money-centre banks) and the unlisted operating businesses 1.28; rechecked at 20 November prices, still 0.98. One local 5-year beta found (StockAnalysis 0.87). No WACC: the holding company has no debt, and the group's borrowings are LB Finance's funding.

**Growth check**

Profit kept × ROE = 74.1% × 11.5% = 8.5% supported. The methods assume 4% / 5% / 6% long-run, all below it and below the 12.24% bond yield.

**Business tests (2 of 4, unchanged)**

- Returns: fail. Owners' ROE 11.5% (2025/26), 10.1%, 12.5%, 14.9%, 18.9% in the years before.
- Debt: pass. The holding company has net cash; the group's debt is LB Finance's deposit and bank funding (loans Rs 377bn at September). Royal Ceramics' net debt is 0.55x its equity.
- Steady profit: pass. Owners' profit in each of the last ten years, Rs 9.5–13.2bn over the last five.
- Cash: fail. Only about Rs 4.1bn of the Rs 13.2bn owners' profit reached the holding company as dividends last year; LB Finance's growth absorbs its capital, and Royal Ceramics' operating cash flow is weak.

**Management and plans**

The chairman and the managing director describe a record year with growth spread across sectors, and an outlook of "cautious optimism". The plans are to keep growing LB Finance (with Associated Motor Finance, housing and EV lending, and an entry into the Philippines), to ride the construction recovery in tiles with more showrooms and better margins, to add value-added packaging, and to keep developing the Greener Water resort. No capital spending budget or payout target is given. Against the half-year figures: finance and tiles are on track (segment profits +27% and +25%), packaging has gone the wrong way (profit −53%), and Greener Water has been delayed again with no new date.

**Shareholders**

Mr Dhammika Perera owns 63.5% directly and, with Vallibel Investments and Vallibel Leisure, about 80.4%; the Employees' Provident Fund has 9.3%; the public holds 19.5% (15,766 holders, 179 more than in June). The twenty largest holders are the same as in June; the only changes are small sales by the HNB Capital Alliance Quantitative Equity Fund (−0.43mn shares) and DFCC Bank (−0.07mn).

**Buy plan (500 shares)**

- 200 shares up to Rs 59.40
- 150 shares up to Rs 50.50
- 150 shares up to Rs 44.60

Average about Rs 52.29, total about Rs 26,145 (Rs 45,650 at Rs 91.30). Not realistic soon: the share traded Rs 88.20–104.00 from April to September 2026; it was last near Rs 50–58 between March 2024 (Rs 50.50) and mid-2025 (low Rs 56.20 in the June 2025 quarter).

**What would change the view**

Higher: LB Finance keeping ROE above 20% with clean credit; Royal Ceramics' operating businesses earning above 12% on capital; Greener Water's hotel opening or being sold; a lower beta after January's refresh; a higher payout. Lower: credit losses at LB Finance (the Rs 1.9bn receivables impairment this half); a weaker Sampath share price; money put into the Lanka Walltiles rights issue or the Fortress Resorts without a return; another delay at Greener Water.

**Uncertain or missing**

LB Finance's price (Rs 159) is from a 9 November broker table; the CSE couldn't be reached from this run for a newer one. LB Finance's share count (554mn) is worked out from the 51.75% stake. The cost of the October Fortress purchase isn't in the reports read. Which year the Rs 1.50 dividend paid in the June 2026 quarter belongs to isn't stated. Delmege's book value is unclear (the subsidiary summary and the minority-interest balance don't agree), so it is valued on profit. The group working-capital change isn't recorded because the group figures mix LB Finance's lending with the operating businesses.

management.source: Annual Report 2025/26: Chairman's statement (pp. 20–21), Managing Director's review (pp. 22–25), sector reviews and capitals (pp. 129, 140, 160, 174) and note 14 (p. 301); progress from the interims to 30 June and 30 September 2026. Page numbers are the printed ones. No earlier management section or 2024/25 annual report was available, so the track record checks this year's plans against the half-year figures.
management.takeaway: Management's plan is more of the same: grow LB Finance (now with Associated Motor Finance, and a planned move into the Philippines) and ride the construction recovery through the tile businesses; it gives no capital spending budget or payout target, and the Greener Water hotel keeps slipping.

said.text: A record year: revenue Rs 149.3bn (+22%), profit before tax Rs 30.6bn (+24%), profit after tax Rs 20.9bn (+30%), spread across sectors rather than one business.
Finance (LB Finance) is the largest earner: net interest income +23% to Rs 31.3bn, profit +29% to Rs 14.0bn.
Tiles and bathware recovered with construction: revenue +15% to Rs 50.4bn, profit from continuing operations +58% to Rs 3.5bn.
Consumer goods (Delmege) turned round to a Rs 243mn profit on revenue +35%; packaging grew revenue 21% but margins were squeezed.
Outlook of 'cautious optimism', with inflation, interest rates, the exchange rate and energy and raw material costs named as the risks.

plans.text: LB Finance: prudent growth, digital lending, housing and electric-vehicle finance, and entry into the Philippines (microfinance and auto finance).
Tiles: more showrooms, a wider range, automation and energy savings to lift margins as building activity picks up.
Packaging: value-added printed cartons in Sri Lanka; study paper-sack making in Kenya after doubling the Kenya corrugator to 700 tonnes.
Group: share capabilities across the businesses and pursue regional expansion selectively.
Leisure: keep developing the Greener Water integrated resort in Negombo (a proposed 500 rooms) alongside The Fortress.

LB Finance's purchase of a controlling stake in Associated Motor Finance
More money into Greener Water (cost of the investment Rs 7.35bn, from Rs 6.79bn)
